query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an α + β dual-phase alloy with low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Earlier studies explored redesigning the bulk alloy, which risks compromising its original advantages, and several surface-modification approaches. Traditional thermal spraying and thermal plating produced weak coatings with poor substrate bonding; composite coatings suffered from uneven constituent dispersion and weak interfaces; and laser cladding could generate intermetallic compounds, high residual stresses, cracks, and crazing. Prior refractory high-entropy-alloy studies reported improved hardness and wear resistance, but the broader requirements of compositional homogeneity, strong bonding, mechanical stability, and preservation of TC4’s beneficial properties remain. Formulate one neutral, testable hypothesis for an intervention that could satisfy these requirements. Specify the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A dual-layer coating strategy, in which a TiAl-based transition layer (e.g., near-equiatomic Ti-50Al) is in situ synthesized via laser cladding beneath an HEA top layer, will create a graded interface that enhances adhesion and mechanical stability on TC4 while markedly improving surface hardness and wear resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: TC4 alloy (Ti6Al4V) with an α + β microstructure that exhibits limited surface hardness and high wear susceptibility.
generation.intervention: Employ a sequential laser cladding process: first, deposit a thin, controlled TiAl-based (approximately Ti-50Al composition) transition layer to form a graded interface, followed by an HEA coating optimized for high hardness and wear resistance.
generation.conditions: Laser cladding parameters must be precisely controlled to achieve a smooth compositional gradient (e.g., controlled deposition thickness and temperature) and rapid cooling to avoid undesirable brittle phases; the TiAl composition should be carefully tailored to prevent phase transformation hazards.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous compositional gradient that minimizes thermal expansion mismatches and stress concentrations, thereby enhancing metallurgical bonding between TC4 and the final hard HEA top layer.
generation.mechanism: The TiAl transition layer acts as an effective adhesive interlayer, absorbing thermal and mechanical mismatches; the subsequent HEA layer contributes superior hardness by leveraging solid solution and second-phase strengthening, resulting in improved wear response.
generation.predicted_outcome: TC4 with this dual-layer system will exhibit increased interfacial adhesion, enhanced hardness, and reduced wear rates under high-contact stress compared to untreated TC4, with no significant indicators of phase-induced brittleness.
generation.baseline: Standard, untreated TC4 alloy with inherent poor wear resistance and low surface hardness.
generation.boundary: The approach is valid provided the graded interface remains stable and free from deleterious phase transformations, which must be verified under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The complete suppression of residual stresses and prevention of minor phase transformations at the graded interface remain to be fully quantified through further thermal and mechanical testing.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate TC4 samples with the dual-layer (TiAl transition layer followed by HEA coating). Perform three-point bending tests, hot tensile tests, detailed SEM/EDS and XRD analyses at the graded interface, and wear tests under simulated high-contact stress.
measurements: Interfacial bonding strength and crack initiation via mechanical tests
Phase and compositional gradients at the interface (SEM/EDS, XRD)
Wear rate and hardness measurements of the coated samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the graded interface shows significant phase transformation, residual stress accumulation, or if mechanical tests indicate bonding strength similar to or poorer than untreated TC4, the hypothesis is refuted.

cited_evidence.text: By laser cladding a RHEA coating on the surface of titanium alloy, the advantages of the high strength and plasticity of the titanium alloy can be combined with the corrosion resistance of RHEA, which not only solves the defects of titanium alloy, but also greatly reduces the production cost and consumption in service. At present, there is little research on the corrosion resistance of high-entropy alloys composed of refractory metal elements, but their excellent performance cannot be ignored. Jiang [] et al. prepared TiZrAlNb and TiZrAlNbCo high-entropy alloy coatings on the surface of TC4 titanium alloy using laser cladding technology. Through a study of their microstructure and corrosion resistance, it was found that the TiZrAlNb and TiZrAlNbCo high-entropy alloy coatings were, respectively, BCC and BCC-fcc matrix phases, and were accompanied by a small number of intermetallic compounds; the dendritic crystals of the TiZrAlNbCo alloy coating were much finer than those of the TiZrAlNb alloy coating. Laser cladding (LC) is a method employed to improve the wear resistance and restoration of engineered alloys by reinforcing and restoring the surface. Nevertheless, a significant concern regarding laser cladding coatings is the non-uniform dispersion of reinforcements and the occurrence of fractures, both of which have a substantial impact on the qualities of the coating. Novel techniques employing optimized laser processing parameters and powdered alloy components have been devised to tackle this issue [,,,]. Preheating and post-heating are techniques employed to produce crack-free coatings in laser cladding. However, the utilization of these techniques is limited. Alternative methodologies need to be explored, and ultrasonic vibration is a particularly promising technique to address the limitations of the laser cladding process [,,,,,,,]. Multiple studies have been undertaken using ultrasonic vibration-assisted laser cladding. Zhou et al. [] performed studies on Inconel 718; the micrographs and mechanical properties of material produced using ultrasonic vibration-assisted laser cladding were evaluated using amplitudes of 10, 15, 20, and 25 µm. High entropy alloys (HEA) are usually composed of 5 or more metallic elements in which the proportion of each element is between 5% and 35% (atomic fraction) [,]. The high entropy effect of HEAs is beneficial for the formation of simple solid solution and inhibits the formation of complex intermetallic compounds. HEAs have excellent properties, such as high strength, high ductility, etc. which are suitable for structural applications [,]. Research has been carried out on the preparation of HEA layers on the substrate of common steel [,]. For example a layer of CrMnFeCoNi was made on the surface of Q235 steel by laser cladding []. Also, on the surface of Q235 steel a layer of CoCr2FeNiMox was made to achieve high wear resistance []. However, the hardness of some HEAs is low and does not satisfy hardness and wear resistance requirements of agriculture knives []. So, the addition of hard ceramic particles becomes an effective method to increase hardness and wear resistance of HEAs [,].
